questions.q: What is the main problem with chemical pesticides, per the summary?
a: They kill far more than the targeted pest
They are too costly for most small farms
They break down before they can help
They work only against plant diseases
questions.why: Lesson 1 says pesticides almost never target unwanted pests alone.

questions.q: What happened after the Forest Service sprayed DDT for spruce budworm?
a: Predators of spider mites died, so the mites exploded
The forest recovered within a single season
The budworm grew resistant and returned
Other insects moved in and restored balance
questions.why: Lesson 1 recounts the 1956 spraying and the spider mite outbreak that followed.

questions.q: How did DDT reach people who never handled it?
a: Through alfalfa fed to chickens and eaten as eggs
Through drinking water from nearby lakes
Through mosquito bites in the region
Through clothing shipped from the farms
questions.why: Lesson 2 traces DDT from alfalfa to chickens to eggs to people.

questions.q: What did the summary say even low DDT levels can do?
a: Damage liver cells at around five parts per million
Improve crop yields slightly over time
Cause immediate paralysis in adults
Have no measurable effect on people
questions.why: Lesson 2 says five parts per million can make liver cells disintegrate.

questions.q: What two solutions does Carson recommend?
a: Education and biological alternatives to pesticides
Bans and heavy financial penalties
Genetic engineering and better irrigation
Crop rotation and chemical fertilizers
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls for education and less intrusive pest controls.
